channel.description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

item.title: [6] Observation of giant acoustoelectric currents in graphene on lead magnesium niobate–lead titanate
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Sarah S. Bedair, Reza Abdolvand

Authors: Hamed Atashbar, Hakhamanesh Mansoorzare, Tara Jabegu, et al.

Score 6/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relevant to 2D materials and electronics studies in condensed matter.

Tags: #graphene #acoustoelectronics #2Dmaterials

Abstract: Acoustoelectric devices can convert radio-frequency-driven acoustic signals into electronic responses and are useful for energy harvesting and various sensing applications. Here, the authors report the integration of graphene with a lead magnesium niobate–lead titanate surface acoustic wave platform, showing enhanced acoustoelectric currents and responsivity.
